# Owner directives (highest priority; supersede roadmap/CI/portability wording)

1. **macOS only initially.** Apple Silicon, macOS 13+. No Linux or Windows code, CI jobs, runners, shims, packaging or portability work until the owner lifts this.
2. Keep platform code isolated behind `platform/` interfaces (clean seams only; no stubs or ports for other OSes).
3. CI/dev scripts target macOS only. Skip any roadmap item for Linux/Windows (M11, M12) and cross-platform CI matrices.

4. **Full Rust port, owner direction2026-10-14.** Stop the former C implementation queue. Port all first-party application/platform/UI/parser/raster/document/animation/MCP code and in-repo development/test tooling to Rust, then complete the existing product finish line. This supersedes the C17 language/build lock and the former two-implementation-worker ceiling. Use as many useful disjoint Luna codex exec workers as available allowance/resources permit; preserve one writer per module and coordinator-only shared integration. Existing subscription allowance only, no extra credits/API billing. Preserve the current C code, unfinished candidates and evidence as migration references; no delete/reset or false completion claim. macOS13+ AppleSilicon, MPL2, custom UI, owned source-preserving SVG/XML parser/rasterizer, minimal reviewed/pinned dependencies, and no GPL editor source remain locked. Broad UI/E2E at the final stage; focused correctness checks continue.

impl PatternTickets {
    /// Borrows the builder until the tile render ends. The caller then drops the
    /// request and publishes same-job output through `complete_mapped`.
    pub fn request_mapped_static<'a>(
        &mut self,
        builder: &'a SceneBuilder,
        draft: &DraftToken,
        source: &DecodeSource<'_>,
        child: SceneId,
        descriptor: PatternDescriptor,
        mapping: PatternMapping,
        shape: ShapeId,
        channel: PaintChannel,
        job: &RasterJob,
        control: &mut dyn WorkControl,
    ) -> Result<StaticPatternRequest<'a>> {
        builder.draft_index(draft)?;
        let request_identity = builder.static_request_child(child)?;
        let view = builder.traversal_scene(child)?;
        let viewport = view
            .viewport
            .ok_or_else(|| invalid(descriptor.error_offset))?;
        crate::validate::viewport(viewport)?;
        // Original C's tile viewport: raster dimensions, origin zero, tile
        // extent and preserveAspectRatio=none. No fabricated parent viewport.
        if viewport.width != descriptor.width
            || viewport.height != descriptor.height
            || viewport.view_x != 0.
            || viewport.view_y != 0.
            || viewport.view_width != descriptor.tile_width
            || viewport.view_height != descriptor.tile_height
            || !viewport.aspect.none
        {
            return Err(invalid(descriptor.error_offset));
        }
        let tables = view.raster_tables(viewport);
        validate_mask_closure(tables, &mut [None; 64], 0, &mut 0, control)?;
        let request = self.request_mapped_view(
            builder, draft, source, child, view, descriptor, mapping, shape, channel, job, control,
        )?;
        let scope = StaticScope {
            generation: builder.generation(),
            job: job.owner_identity(),
            draft: draft.nonce,
            request: request_identity,
            ticket: request.ticket,
        };
        Ok(StaticPatternRequest {
            ticket: request.ticket,
            descriptor,
            child: StaticPatternView {
                input: RasterInput::static_child(tables, scope),
            },
        })
    }
}
fn validate_mask_closure(
    view: SceneView<'_, Viewport, ()>,
    stack: &mut [Option<SceneId>; 64],
    depth: usize,
    visits: &mut usize,
    control: &mut dyn WorkControl,
) -> Result<()> {
    control.checkpoint().map_err(stopped)?;
    if depth == stack.len() || *visits >= 65536 {
        return Err(crate::types::limit(LimitKind::Masks));
    }
    if stack[..depth].contains(&Some(view.id)) {
        return Err(invalid(0));
    }
    *visits = visits
        .checked_add(1)
        .ok_or_else(crate::memory::arithmetic)?;
    stack[depth] = Some(view.id);
    for mask in view.masks {
        control
            .charge(WorkKind::ReferenceProbe, 1)
            .map_err(stopped)?;
        let child = view
            .scene(mask.content)
            .ok_or_else(|| invalid(mask.source_offset))?;
        crate::validate::viewport(child.viewport)?;
        validate_mask_closure(child, stack, depth + 1, visits, control)?;
    }
    // Also require the initial child sealed (scene lookup checks serial/seal).
    view.scene(view.id).ok_or_else(|| invalid(0))?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Original [min x, min y, max x, max y], including zero extent.
/// Rejects overflowed extents even when each coordinate itself is finite.
pub fn ordered_bounds_extent(bounds: [f64; 4]) -> Option<[f64; 2]> {
    if !bounds.into_iter().all(f64::is_finite) {
        return None;
    }
    let extent = [bounds[2] - bounds[0], bounds[3] - bounds[1]];
    extent
        .into_iter()
        .all(|v| v.is_finite() && v >= 0.)
        .then_some(extent)
}
/// An animation-free read capability. No raw scene/ready conversion or arbitrary

impl<'a> RasterInput<'a> {

        self.tables.viewport

    pub fn source(self) -> &'a [u8] {

/// Same scalar coordinates/lattice/edge data as SampleInput. The lower engine
/// changes its input type and propagates Result; its math and cost stay unchanged.
pub struct CommonSampleInput<'a> {
    pub resources: &'a dyn CommonKernelResources,
    pub active_edges: &'a [u32],
    pub local_edges: &'a [Edge],
    pub dash_seams: &'a [bool],
    pub dash_cache: ValidatedDashView<'a>,
    pub px: f64,
    pub py: f64,
    pub paint_x: f64,
    pub paint_y: f64,
}
impl CommonSampleInput<'_> {
    pub fn validate(&self, view: RasterInput<'_>, control: &mut dyn WorkControl) -> Result<()> {
        if !self.dash_cache.matches_source(view.source_owner()) {
            return Err(invalid(0));
        }
        if ![self.px, self.py, self.paint_x, self.paint_y]
            .into_iter()
            .all(f64::is_finite)
            || self.dash_seams.len() != self.local_edges.len()
        {
            return Err(invalid(0));
        }
        control.checkpoint().map_err(stopped)?;
        for index in self.active_edges {
            control.charge(WorkKind::Edge, 1).map_err(stopped)?;
            if *index as usize >= view.edges().len() {
                return Err(invalid(0));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    /// No precharge or aftercharge substitute: the actual resource receives the
    /// caller's control, including while traversing stops/pattern samples.
    pub fn paint_sample(
        &self,
        paint: &Paint,
        stops: &[PaintStop],
        control: &mut dyn WorkControl,
    ) -> Result<[u8; 4]> {
        control.checkpoint().map_err(stopped)?;
        self.resources
            .paint_sample(paint, stops, self.paint_x, self.paint_y, control)
    }
}

/// Guard before calling the lower renderer. Its output remains in the same job.
pub fn render_common_pattern(
    kernel: &mut dyn CommonRasterKernel,
    request: &StaticPatternRequest<'_>,
    options: RenderOptions,
    job: &mut RasterJob,
    control: &mut dyn WorkControl,
) -> Result<JobRenderOutput> {
    let input = request.child.input();
    input.validate_job(job, control)?;
    let output = kernel.render_flat(
        input,
        TableRange {
            first: 0,
            count: input.shapes().len(),
        },
        options,
        job,
        control,
    )?;
    let validation = output.validate(job).and_then(|()| {
        if Some(output.generation) != input.static_generation()
            || output.width != request.descriptor.width
            || output.height != request.descriptor.height
        {
            Err(invalid(request.descriptor.error_offset))
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    });
    if let Err(error) = validation {
        if job.require_pool(output.pixels, RasterPool::Output).is_ok()
            && job.slice(output.pixels).is_ok()
        {
            job.release(output.pixels)?;
        }
        return Err(error);
    }
    Ok(output)
}

    request: TextDecodeRequest<'_, '_>,
    builder: &mut SceneBuilder,
    draft: &DraftToken,
    control: &mut dyn WorkControl,
) -> Result<bool> {

    fn validate_media_draft(&self, draft: &DraftToken, scene: SceneId) -> Result<()> {

        }
        Ok(())
    }
